contributions: Introduces four fundamental sources of uncertainty in decision making: outcome, model, state, and interaction uncertainty
Presents algorithms implemented in Julia prioritizing interpretability over efficiency
Organizes computational methods (explicit programming, supervised learning, optimization, planning, reinforcement learning) within a unified decision-making framework
Demonstrates applications across aerospace, autonomous vehicles, healthcare, finance, environmental monitoring, and space exploration
limitations: Algorithm implementations prioritize interpretability over efficiency, so industrial applications may require alternative implementations
Requires mathematical maturity and prior exposure to multivariable calculus, linear algebra, and probability; review material is only provided in appendices
Covers only a selection of methods (planning and reinforcement learning are primary focus) while acknowledging many other approaches exist

methods: The book develops mathematical problem formulations for decision making and provides algorithms to solve them, with all code implemented in the Julia programming language. It organizes content around four types of uncertainty and covers five methodological approaches: explicit programming, supervised learning (behavioral cloning), optimization via simulation-based search, planning with dynamic models, and reinforcement learning where strategies are learned through environment interaction. The target audience is advanced undergraduates and graduate students with prerequisites in multivariable calculus, linear algebra, and probability.
results: As a textbook preface and introduction, the work does not report empirical results or quantitative findings. It outlines the scope and organization of the textbook, presents six real-world application domains (aircraft collision avoidance, automated driving, breast cancer screening, financial consumption/portfolio allocation, distributed wildfire surveillance, and Mars science exploration), and traces the historical interdisciplinary roots of decision-making theory across economics, psychology, neuroscience, and computer science.
tldr: This textbook provides a broad introduction to algorithms for decision making under uncertainty, covering mathematical formulations and computational approaches across diverse real-world applications.
